Policy Name: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)

Required findings: ≥6 months elapsed since prior cervical decompression or fusion at an adjacent level

Significant daily pain causing functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing) AND unremitting radicular pain to shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity resulting in disability

Physical exam demonstrating any of: dermatomal sensory deficit, motor weakness (biceps/triceps), reflex changes, shoulder abduction relief sign, positive Spurling's maneuver, or persistent radicular pain without concordant objective findings

Failure to achieve clinically meaningful improvement after at least two of the following for ≥6 weeks (unless contraindicated): prescription‑strength analgesics/NSAIDs/steroids/gabapentinoids, provider‑directed exercise program, epidural steroid injection or selective nerve root block at the same level

Plain cervical spine X‑rays (including flexion/extension) and advanced imaging confirming successful decompression/fusion at the prior level; MRI/CT of the proposed level showing neural compression (herniated disc, synovial/arachnoid cyst, central/lateral/foraminal stenosis, or osteophytes) concordant with symptoms and exam
No unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorder
Nicotine‑free status: never smoker or abstinent ≥6 weeks with objective cotinine test (serum, urine, or saliva) within normal range

Symptoms of any of the following: upper or lower extremity weakness, numbness or pain; fine motor dysfunction (e.g., difficulty buttoning, handwriting); gait disturbance; new‑onset bowel or bladder dysfunction; frequent falls

Physical exam demonstrating any of: abnormal grip‑release test, ataxic gait, hyperreflexia, Hoffmann sign, Babinski sign, tandem walking ataxia, inverted brachial radial reflex, increased muscle tone/spasticity, clonus, myelopathic hand
MRI or CT showing findings concordant with the clinical picture and caused by cervical spinal cord compression or cervical spinal stenosis
